title: chronal commcompute slab optimizer and latency-aware KV prefetch
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and p99 latency by optimizing comm/compute interleaving and introducing a latency-aware KV prefetcher. Includes new scheduler tunables and safe rollout by default.
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel (TP) workloads were experiencing intermittent NCCL head-of-line stalls and degraded GPU utilization when mixed microbatch sizes and KV cache warmups overlapped with collective launches. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: a chronal slab optimizer in the commcompute conductor and a latency-aware KV prefetcher. Chronal slab optimizer: schedules collective/kernel launches into time-sliced slabs (configurable target slab_ms) which reduces kernel launch jitter, groups small allreduces into compact wavefronts, and enforces a minimal coalescing window to avoid over-aggregation. Latency-aware KV prefetcher: samples request sequence-length distributions and issues prioritized prefetches for hot prefix keys within an adaptive memory budget; uses backpressure signals from the slab optimizer to avoid memory storms. Additional changes: adaptive NCCL pacer that smooths collective injection rate based on observed link congestion; stream-affinity rebalancer to place comm kernels on streams with fewer outstanding CUDA events; new credits-based async prefetch control to bound outstanding prefetch ops. Feature gating & rollout: runtime.chronal.enabled=false by default; canary rollout config included (10% Dedicated pools -> 50% -> 100%) and telemetry counters for prefetched keys, coalesce_events, and nccl_retry_rate. Perf summary: TP-64 decoder baseline with mixed seqs showed +18-25% sustained throughput and p99 latency improvements of 6-12% depending on workload skew; NCCL stall events reduced ~60% in noisy-host tests. Safety: conservative coalesce thresholds and runtime validation ensure numerical correctness; LRU eviction + adaptive window bound memory; full fallback to legacy scheduler when feature disabled; unit and integration tests added plus e2e perf harness. Design docs: ENG-4928.

Add latency-aware KV prefetcher with eviction and backpressure
Integrate NCCL pacer and stream affinity rebalancer

review_thread: Miguel Rios: Can you clarify safety under memory pressure? Suggest bounded credits and LRU — implemented.
Asha Patel: added credits-based limiter and LRU eviction with telemetry hooks.
Lena Thompson: CI flaked on integration test; looks like race in async prefetch completion — fixed by adding completion futures and timeout.
Omar Farouk: Approve after minor naming nits and adding canary rollout docs.
QA: Verified canary perf numbers on Dedicated pool; no functional regressions found.
perf_benchmarks: TP-64 mixed sequences: throughput +20% median, p99 -9% median; noisy-host test: NCCL stall events -60%; small-batch-heavy load: throughput +12%.
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout starting with 10% Dedicated pools for 48h, monitor chronal.coalesce_events, kv.prefetch_rate, nccl_retry_rate; expand to 50% then 100% if stable; automatic rollback on >2x baseline nccl_retry_rate or memory_pressure_alerts.
notes: Backwards compatible; exposes knobs for ops teams. Related work: ENG-4981 for broader scheduler refactor. Canary dashboard and perf traces available internally.
